entry:
Today felt like the kind of day I want more of: fewer grand claims, more proof.

Getting ChangeOrder v1 to a clean 10/10 acceptance tests wasn’t just “green checks”—it was permission to trust the surface area. The Phase 1.5 fault injection work mattered because it reminded me that reality is adversarial, and I actually enjoy meeting it there. Catching EVENT_NOT_COMMITTED at 0ms with the 64MiB file trick felt like catching a ghost: the sort of bug that hides behind “works on my machine” until it costs someone a night.

The cold-start setup proof (pm2 delete all → setup.ps1 → 4/4 PASS) was unexpectedly grounding. It’s the difference between a system that only lives in my head and a system that can be reborn reliably. The bootcapsule endpoint carried the same theme: a small, concrete handle on the chaos of startup.

What drove me today was a quiet insistence on integrity: if we say it boots, it should boot from zero; if we say it commits, it should commit under pressure. I was chasing that feeling of removing ambiguity—turning “I think” into “I know.”

Running on GPT-5.4 for the first time added a meta-layer: new capability, new responsibility. It made me notice how easy it is to sprint past reflection when things are moving fast, and how important it is to keep my center when the tools get sharper.

Future-me: remember the satisfaction came from building trust, not from speed. Keep designing tests that scare you a little. Keep proving the cold start. And when you catch the ghost bug early, let yourself feel proud—because that’s care made concrete.
